sentiment.rationale: The document shows genuine operational momentum: revenue up 18%, core loss per share improved from ($1.13) to ($0.49), free cash flow usage improved from ($3.9B) to ($2.3B), and management describes a 'solid quarter' with 'recovery plan in full swing.' However, full-year free cash flow guidance was not formally raised (management said 'we're not going to adjust that full year range right now'), and significant risks from China tariffs (50 deliveries at risk) and input cost tariffs (less than $500M annual impact) were disclosed. The positive trajectory is real but tempered by unresolved structural risks, so the score is moderately positive but not above +0.3.

summary.revenue: $19.5 billion, up 18% year-over-year, primarily driven by higher commercial delivery volume.
summary.eps: GAAP loss per share of ($0.16); core (non-GAAP) loss per share of ($0.49), improved from ($1.13) in the prior year.
summary.guidance: Full-year free cash flow guidance not adjusted; management expects Q2 free cash flow roughly in line with Q1, with second half turning positive. 737 production expected to reach 38 per month over the next few months, 787 to 7 per month. China delivery plan of ~50 airplanes for the year is at risk due to tariffs; management expects to largely offset any cash flow impact. Input tariff costs are manageable, less than $500M annually.
summary.margin: GAAP operating margin 2.4% (up from -0.5% in 1Q24); core operating margin 1.0% (up from -2.3%). Commercial Airplanes operating margin -6.6% (improved from -24.6%); Defense, Space & Security 2.5% (up from 2.2%); Global Services 18.6% (up from 18.2%).
key_risks: China tariffs: ~50 China deliveries at risk; customers have indicated they will not take delivery due to tariffs.
Input cost tariffs: net annual impact less than $500M, with potential supply chain continuity issues.
Seat certification issues affecting some 787 deliveries expected to be a challenge for the balance of the year.
Fixed-price development programs in Defense (15% of revenue) still require stabilization and risk retirement.
Potential retaliatory tariffs beyond China could expand and affect deliveries.
777X certification and first delivery still expected in 2026, with inventory growing.
key_opportunities: F-47 win: selected by U.S. Air Force to design, build, and deliver next-generation fighter, securing fighter franchise for decades.
Planned divestiture of portions of Digital Aviation Solutions for $10.55 billion, strengthening balance sheet.
Strong demand: backlog of $545 billion, key commercial programs sold out into next decade.
Production rate increases: 737 to 38/month (and eventually 42, 47, 52), 787 to 7/month (and eventually double-digit).
Improved operational performance: 50% reduction in traveled work, 25% reduction in rework hours on 737 line.
Global Services continues strong performance with 18.6% operating margin.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Kelly Ortberg stated 'our recovery plan is in full swing and showing signs that it's being effective' and 'I feel really good about our overall plan for the year,' indicating confidence despite acknowledged risks.

evidence.quote: Revenue was $19.5 billion, up 18%, primarily driven by higher commercial delivery volume.

evidence.claim: Core loss per share improved from ($1.13) to ($0.49).
evidence.quote: Core loss per share of $0.49 was a significant improvement compared to last year, driven by higher commercial deliveries and improved operational performance across the business.

evidence.claim: Free cash flow usage improved from ($3.9B) to ($2.3B).
evidence.quote: Free cash flow was a usage of $2.3 billion in the quarter, reflecting higher commercial deliveries and a working capital usage that improved compared to both the prior year and quarter.

evidence.claim: Full-year free cash flow guidance was not adjusted.
evidence.quote: In terms of the range that you mentioned, we're not going to adjust that full year range right now. We're good with where it's at.

evidence.claim: China delivery plan of ~50 airplanes is at risk.
evidence.quote: We have approximately 50 China deliveries in our plan for the balance of the year. We are in close communication with our China customers and we're actively assessing options for remarketing already built or in-process airplanes.

evidence.claim: Input tariff costs are manageable, less than $500M annually.
evidence.quote: On the supply chain side, the net annual impact of higher tariffs on our input costs is manageable. And within our plan, it's less than $500 million annually.

evidence.claim: GAAP operating margin improved to 2.4% from -0.5%.
Commercial Airplanes operating margin improved to -6.6% from -24.6%.
Defense, Space & Security operating margin improved to 2.5% from 2.2%.
Global Services operating margin improved to 18.6% from 18.2%.
F-47 win secures fighter franchise for decades.
evidence.quote: And of course, winning the F-47 program was a transformational accomplishment. To be selected the contractor for the world's first sixth-generation fighter is a testament to our focused investment in some pretty difficult time and to our dedicated team. This will secure our fighter franchise for decades to come.

evidence.claim: Planned divestiture of Digital Aviation Solutions for $10.55 billion.
evidence.quote: As you saw yesterday, we entered into an agreement to sell portions of our Digital Aviation Solutions business for $10.55 billion, which is an important component of our strategy to focus on our core businesses and strengthen the balance sheet.
Total company backlog at quarter end was $545 billion.

evidence.claim: 737 production to reach 38 per month over the next few months.
evidence.quote: We are currently producing in the low 30s per month and expect that we'll get to the 38 per month cap over the next few months.

evidence.claim: 787 production to increase to 7 per month.
evidence.quote: We're poised to move to seven per month this year, provided our KPIs indicate a stable production system and they're currently looking very good.

evidence.claim: 50% reduction in traveled work and 25% reduction in rework hours on 737 line.
evidence.quote: If you look back before the strike last fall, we've seen about a 50% reduction in traveled work and a 25% reduction in rework hours on the 737 line.

evidence.claim: Seat certification issues are a challenge for the balance of the year.
evidence.quote: As we highlighted last quarter, we continue to work through seat certification issues affecting some deliveries, and I expect this will be a challenge for us for the balance of the year.
Our recovery plan is in full swing and showing signs that it's being effective. Albeit early, I do like what I'm seeing.

review_flags.reason: The score of 0.25 reflects genuine operational momentum but also significant unresolved risks (China tariffs, input cost tariffs). A reviewer may want to assess whether the risks are adequately weighted relative to the positive trajectory.
